newsitem.title: USA: Silent film star Laura La Plante dies.
newsitem.headline: Silent film star Laura La Plante dies.

text.p: Laura La Plante, a leading lady in Universal Pictures silent movies of the 1920s, died on Monday, the Motion Picture & Television Hospital said. She was 92.
A spokeswoman at the hospital in suburban Woodland Hills declined to give the cause of her death, but the family requested donations be made to the Alzheimer's Association in her memory.
Born in St. Louis in 1904, La Plante began acting at 15 in comedies. Her first break came in 1921, when she appeared in "The Old Swimmin' Hole," winning a contract with Universal.
In 1923, she was named a Wampas Baby star and headed a cast of numerous films, initially Westerns, and later comedies and melodramas.
Billed as a girl-next-door type, she is best remembered as the heroine of Gothic dramas such as "The Cat and the Canary" and as Magnolia in the 1929 version of "Showboat."

She retired in the early 1930s after appearing in 50 films and serials and married Warner Bros. producer Irving Asher in 1934. Twice she came out of retirement to play character parts -- in 1946 in "Little Mister Jim" and in 1957 in "Spring Reunion."
Her husband died in 1985 and Asher lived at the Motion Picture & Television Fund's retirement community from 1989.
She is survived by a son, a daughter and a grandson.
